blinding_guess.why: The robot_description read path looks ordinary. How a particular .dae renders depends on file contents this snapshot cannot show: mesh_loader.cpp skips the Assimp root-node transform (line 223, so a COLLADA up_axis is not applied), rescales by <unit meter>, and assigns submesh materials by index into scene->mMeshes (line 548) although submeshes are created in node-traversal order. Any of these could misrender a specific mesh, but nothing in the snapshot names create_body.dae.

notes: ROS 1 (groovy): all QoS fields null by rule. Both packet elements are consumed; nothing is provided, so declares and not_declared are empty. param:robot_description: the parameter name is the default value of the user-editable 'Robot Description' property (robot_model_display.cpp:82), so it can be changed in the display config; it is read with a relative NodeHandle getParam and then searchParam, as a string holding URDF XML (no ROS message type, no definition hash). resource:package://create_description/meshes/create_body.dae: the snapshot never names this resource or the create_description package; rviz receives mesh URLs at run time from the URDF <mesh filename> (robot_link.cpp:443) and fetches them via resource_retriever (package:// URLs), so it is not listed in references. The mesh is attached to the link's scene node at the URDF visual/collision origin, and the link-to-tf-frame mapping (optional 'TF Prefix' property) is decided at run time from the URDF content, so frame is null for both ports rather than per_message. units 'meters' for the mesh port is the code's stated normalisation target for COLLADA files with a <unit meter> attribute (default scale 1.0 when absent); URDF <mesh scale> is also applied (robot_link.cpp:441). No rate or definition file applies to either element.
